question: Which of the following viruses can easily cause a latent infection ?:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Cytomegalovirus" -> "infection of host cells" -> "integration into host genome" -> "latency in host cells" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Parotitis" -> "infection of salivary glands" -> "acute inflammation" -> "resolution without latency" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Rage" -> "infection of nervous system" -> "acute neurological symptoms" -> "no latency" -> 5%
CHAIN: "Hepatitis A" -> "infection of liver cells" -> "acute hepatitis" -> "resolution without latency" -> 10%
analysis: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) is known for its ability to establish latent infections in the host. It is a member of the Herpesviridae family, which is characterized by their capacity to remain dormant within the body and reactivate under certain conditions. In contrast, Parotitis (commonly caused by the mumps virus), Rage (rabies virus), and Hepatitis A do not typically establish latent infections. Hepatitis A is an acute infection, and rabies is a progressive, acute infection that does not become latent.
